docs.purpose: Receives payment-status events directly from the payment provider — checkout completed, subscription created, updated or cancelled, invoice paid or failed — and updates the corresponding user's paid-access status. This is the mechanism that actually turns a subscriber's access on or off after billing is processed.
docs.data_story: It reads 3 tables — `entitlements`, `user_profiles` and `logic_variables` and writes `stripe_webhook_events` and `entitlements`. Its response shape is **unmeasured** as a pick-by-name whitelist — it passes rows through, spreads a row into a computed object, or assembles the payload dynamically, so there is no single list naming what leaves the server. **Nothing in this repository calls it.** That is the state this registry exists to make visible, not a claim that it is dead — a caller could be a bookmark, an external system, or a path built from variables.
docs.under_126: Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `WEBHOOK`. It declares its signature verification, its closed `events[]` set, its replay guard, its ordering watermark and its behaviour on an unknown event. Its `consumers[]` is the field that matters most here: today it is empty, and the orphan panel renders that as a red row rather than leaving it to be discovered years later.

notes: Also cites docs/specs/00-architecture/116_multi_product_architecture.md §4. Verifies the Stripe-Signature header against STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET before trusting any payload and enforces a 1MB body cap as a DoS guard on this public route. The dedup INSERT into stripe_webhook_events and the entitlements upsert run in one transaction so a provider retry cannot double-apply an event. The response body is the provider-required { received: true } shape, not the app's standard envelope. A safeLogError wrapper guarantees a logging failure can never roll back the dedup transaction, which would otherwise forge an infinite retry loop. consumers: [] is expected — the caller is Stripe itself, external to this repo. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: CLOSED SET OF HANDLED event.type VALUES (classifyEvent switch, :177-280) — 6 handled types plus a no-op default: (1) 'checkout.session.completed' :179 -> newStatus 'active', identity from client_reference_id ?? metadata.user_id (:194), product from session.metadata.product when it validates against PRODUCTS else the OD5 default (:190, :196-197, :424-428); (2) 'customer.subscription.created' :203 and (3) 'customer.subscription.updated' :204 -> newStatus via mapStripeSubStatus (:211; src/lib/stripe/client.ts:58-69: active->active, past_due->past_due, unpaid->expired, EVERYTHING ELSE INCLUDING 'canceled' -> null/no-op), price from items.data[0] (:217); (4) 'invoice.payment_succeeded' :224 -> 'active', resolveProductViaSubscription true (:238); (5) 'invoice.payment_failed' :241 -> 'past_due' (:244,:251); (6) 'customer.subscription.deleted' :254 -> 'expired' (:258) — the SOLE canonical access-revocation signal (:139-143, :207-210); (7) default :268-278 -> all-null outcome, dedup row committed, 200 no-op. COLUMN MUTATION ANSWER: this route mutates NO user_profiles column — user_profiles is READ ONLY (:384-387); the header states this explicitly at :371-373 and I verified it by reading all 503 lines. The entitlements columns it can write are the 8 listed in `writes`. TWO DEFECTS A REVIEWER MUST KNOW: (a) the safeLogError wrapper (:75-81) exists specifically so a throwing logger cannot roll back the dedup row and forge an infinite Stripe retry loop — but the logWarn calls at :439 and :445 run INSIDE that same transaction UNWRAPPED, as does resolvePriceProduct's logWarn (src/lib/entitlements/index.ts:317, :325) reached from :450; the stated fence is therefore incomplete. (b) the 413 check compares `rawBody.length` — a JavaScript string length in UTF-16 code units — against a constant named MAX_BODY_BYTES (:310-311), so multi-byte payloads are undercounted; and request.text() at :292 has already buffered the whole body before the check runs, so the cap does not bound peak memory (the comment at :306-309 concedes this). CENSUS AGREEMENT: matches exactly (reads entitlements + user_profiles + logic_variables; writes stripe_webhook_events + entitlements). | Idempotency: GUARDED — verdict: sound. The dedup INSERT (:337-342) and the entitlement upsert (:458) execute inside ONE withTransaction (:330), so (a) a concurrent Stripe retry that loses the ON CONFLICT race returns early at :343-348 and applies nothing, and (b) if the side effect throws, the dedup row rolls back WITH it and Stripe's retry can legitimately re-process. Three additional write-side fences live in the upsert's WHERE clause (src/lib/entitlements/index.ts:171-173): an out-of-order watermark keyed on Stripe's own event.created (route :457, NOT wall clock), a deletion fence (status IS DISTINCT FROM 'cancelled_pending_deletion'), and a superseded-subscription fence (non-'active' events apply only when stripe_subscription_id matches). CAVEAT worth flagging: the dedup row is COMMITTED even on the three no-apply paths — unknown/no-op event type (:350-356), no user resolved (:390-401) and non-uuid user (:402-411) — so those events are permanently consumed and Stripe will never retry them; this is deliberate (comments at :352-354, :391-393) but means an orphan even
